(Hinesville, Georgia) | college = *[[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] (2017–2018) *[[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] (2019–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 9 | draft_team = [[Sacramento Kings]] | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2023|end}} | team1 = [[Sacramento Kings]] | years2 = {{nbay|2024|full=y}} | team2 = [[Toronto Raptors]] | years3 = {{nbay|2024|end}}–present | team3 = [[Miami Heat]] | highlights = * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball champions|NCAA champion]] ([[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2021]]) * [[Naismith Defensive Player of the Year Award|Naismith Defensive Player of the Year]] (2021) * [[NABC Defensive Player of the Year]] (2021) * [[Lefty Driesell Award]] (2021) * Third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[Associated Press|AP]], [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]], ''[[The Sporting News|SN]]'' ([[2021 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2021]]) * First-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12]] (2021) * Third-team All-Big 12 (2020) * Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year (2021) * 2× Big 12 All-Defensive Team (2020, 2021) * Big 12 Newcomer of the Year (2020) * Big 12 All-Newcomer Team (2020) }} '''Davion De'Monte Earl Mitchell''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|d|eɪ|v|i|ˌ|ɒ|n}} {{respell|DAY|vee|on}};{{cite press release |author= |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 17, 2024}} born September 5, 1998), nicknamed '''Off-Night''', is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Miami Heat]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]] and the [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor Bears]]. He was taken ninth overall in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]]. ==Early life== Mitchell attended [[Liberty County High School (Georgia)|Liberty County High School]] in [[Hinesville, Georgia]]. As a junior, he averaged 24.2 points, 7.1 assists and 2.9 steals per game, leading his team to its first Class 4A state title. Mitchell was named ''[[Savannah Morning News]]'' Player of the Year.{{cite web |last=Knight |first=Dennis |title=Boys Basketball Player of the Year: Davion Mitchell, Liberty County |url=https://www.savannahnow.com/article/20160528/SPORTS/305289837 |website=[[Savannah Morning News]] |access-date=October 28, 2020 |date=May 28, 2016 |archive-date=November 3, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201103021255/https://www.savannahnow.com/article/20160528/SPORTS/305289837 |url-status=dead }} In his senior season, he averaged 23.8 points, 5.3 rebounds and 5.2 assists per game. Mitchell competed for the Georgia Stars on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit.{{cite web |last=Werner |first=John |title=Davion Mitchell brings tenacity to Baylor D |url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/davion-mitchell-brings-tenacity-to-baylor-d/article_834d3201-81e0-55bd-95ec-263af0b7e38c.html |website=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]] |access-date=October 9, 2020 |date=February 14, 2020}} A consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] over offers from [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]], [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]], [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]] and [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]], among others.{{cite web |last=Kramer |first=Daniel |title=Davion Mitchell to Auburn: Tigers Land 4-Star PG Prospect |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2579576-davion-mitchell-to-auburn-tigers-land-4-star-pg-prospect |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=October 28, 2020 |date=October 15, 2015}} ==College career== As a freshman at [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], Mitchell averaged 3.7 points and 1.9 assists per game as a backup [[point guard]] to [[Jared Harper]].{{cite web |last=Stevens |first=Matthew |title=Davion Mitchell to transfer away from Auburn after one season |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/auburn/2018/03/29/davion-mitchell-transfer-away-auburn-after-one-season/471330002/ |website=[[Montgomery Advertiser]] |access-date=October 9, 2020 |date=March 29, 2018}} Following the season, he transferred to [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] and sat out his next season due to [[NCAA]] transfer rules.{{cite web |last=Berger |first=Matthew |title=Baylor basketball adds transfer Davion Mitchell |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/2018/04/16/baylor-basketball-adds-transfer-davion-mitchell/ |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |date=April 15, 2018}} During his [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] year, he improved his all-around game and studied film on guards like [[Kyle Lowry]] and [[Jalen Brunson]]. During his sophomore season, Mitchell was a starter on one of the top teams in the nation.{{cite web |last=Moore |first=CJ |title=Jared Butler and Davion Mitchell are driving one another to greatness at Baylor |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1651984/2020/03/05/jared-butler-and-davion-mitchell-are-driving-one-another-to-greatness-at-baylor/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=October 9, 2020 |date=March 5, 2020}} On December 18, 2019, he posted a season-high 19 points, four assists and four steals in a 91–63 win over [[UT Martin Skyhawks men's basketball|UT Martin]].{{cite web |last=Werner |first=John |title=Mitchell guides Baylor men to 91-63 romp over Skyhawks in Houston |url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/mitchell-guides-baylor-men-to-91-63-romp-over-skyhawks-in-houston/article_371b6894-b9cb-558e-99ad-8dc09fe33e6a.html |website=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]] |access-date=October 9, 2020 |date=December 18, 2019}} As a sophomore, Mitchell averaged 9.9 points and 3.8 assists per game. He was named [[Big 12]] Newcomer of the Year, while earning third-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12]], All-Defensive and All-Newcomer Team honors.{{cite web |last=Mastandrea |first=Matthew |title=Baylor Basketball: Davion Mitchell poised for career year with Bears in 2020-21 |url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2020/09/18/baylor-basketball-davion-mitchell-poised-career-year-bears-2020-21/ |website=Busting Brackets |access-date=October 9, 2020 |date=September 18, 2020}} In his junior season, Mitchell became an improved shooter and passer.{{cite web |last=Ham |first=James |title=How NBA draft prospect Mitchell fits both Warriors and Kings |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/kings/2021-nba-draft-how-baylors-davion-mitchell-fits-warriors-kings |website=[[NBC Sports]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=July 14, 2021}} He scored a career-high 31 points and seven three-pointers in a 107–59 win over [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] on January 27, 2021.{{cite web |last=Chamblee |first=Will |title=Davion Mitchell is red hot for Baylor on both sides of the court |url=https://baylorlariat.com/2021/02/17/davion-mitchell-is-red-hot-for-baylor-on-both-sides-of-the-court/ |website=[[The Baylor Lariat]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=February 17, 2021}} Mitchell helped Baylor win its first national championship, recording 15 points, six rebounds and five assists in an 86–70 win against previously undefeated [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] in the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|title game]].{{cite web |last=Dominitz |first=Nathan |title=The stuff of legends: Savannah-area star Mitchell leads Baylor to national championship |url=https://www.savannahnow.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2021/04/06/baylor-basketball-national-champion-guard-davion-mitchell-of-hinesville-beats-gonzaga-for-ncaa-title/7104206002/ |website=[[Savannah Morning News]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=April 6, 2021}} He received the [[Naismith Defensive Player of the Year Award]], [[NABC Defensive Player of the Year]] award and the [[Lefty Driesell Award]] as the top defensive player in the nation.{{cite web |last1=Houmard |first1=Celeste |last2=Aleman |first2=Christian |date=April 1, 2021 |title=Baylor's Davion Mitchell scores Lefty Driesell, NABC, Naismith defensive player of the year awards |url=https://www.kcentv.com/article/sports/baylors-mitchell-awarded-2021-lefty-driesell-national-defensive-player-of-the-year/500-61143bff-06a2-4e0c-8e22-288f90810c56 |access-date=July 21, 2021 |website=[[KCEN-TV]]}} Mitchell earned Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year and first-team All-Big 12 honors.{{cite web |last=Sulkowski |first=Frank |title=Liberty County's Davion Mitchell named Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year |url=https://www.wjcl.com/article/liberty-countys-davion-mitchell-named-big-12-defensive-player-of-the-year/35774783# |website=[[WJCL (TV)|WJCL]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=March 8, 2021}} On April 13, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Boone |first=Kyle|title=Baylor star Davion Mitchell declares after helping lead Bears to first national championship |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2021-nba-draft-baylor-star-davion-mitchell-declares-after-helping-lead-bears-to-first-national-championship/|website=[[CBSSports.com]] |access-date=April 23, 2021 |date=April 14, 2021}} ==Professional career== === Sacramento Kings (2021–2024) === Mitchell was selected with the ninth overall pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web |last=Nicholson |first=Nikki |date=July 29, 2021 |title=Kings Select Davion Mitchell in the First Round of NBA Draft 2021 |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-select-davion-mitchell-first-round-nba-draft-2021 |access-date=May 2, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On August 5, 2021, he signed his [[NBA salary cap|rookie-scale contract]] with the Kings.{{cite web |last=Nicholson |first=Nikki |date=August 5, 2021 |title=Kings Sign Davion Mitchell |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-davion-mitchell |access-date=May 2, 2023 |website=nba.com}} Mitchell helped the Kings win the [[2021 NBA Summer League]] championship and was named [[NBA Summer League]] MVP alongside [[Cam Thomas (basketball)|Cam Thomas]]. Mitchell was also selected to the All-NBA Summer League First Team.{{Cite web |last=Conway |first=Tyler |date=August 19, 2021 |title=Kings' Davion Mitchell, Nets' Cameron Thomas Named Co-MVPs of 2021 NBA Summer League |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10010571-kings-davion-mitchell-nets-cameron-thomas-named-co-mvps-of-2021-nba-summer-league |access-date=November 25, 2024 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}} On October 20, Mitchell made his NBA debut, recording two points, three rebounds and three assists in a 124–121 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{Cite web |last=Peterson |first=Anne M. |date=October 21, 2021 |title=BARNES HAS 36 AND THE KINGS SPOIL PORTLAND'S OPENER 124-121 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100013 |access-date=May 2, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On March 20, 2022, he scored a career-high 28 points, alongside three rebounds and nine assists, in a 127–124 overtime loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{Cite web |last=Wagaman |first=Michael |date=March 21, 2022 |title=SHAMET HITS KEY 3-POINTER IN OT, SUNS RALLY TO BEAT KINGS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022101066 |access-date=May 2, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} After [[De'Aaron Fox]] went down with a hand injury near the end of the season, Mitchell started in his place averaging 18.6 points and 8.9 assists on 45.8% shooting in 38.1 minutes played for those games.{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Marcus D. |title=Sacramento Kings guard Davion Mitchell looks to add a key skill to his game this offseason |url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/article277023378.html |access-date=23 March 2025 |work=Sacramento Bee |date=6 July 2023}} In his second season, Mitchell's playing time and scoring decreased as his minutes were spread to new teammates, [[Malik Monk]] and [[Kevin Huerter]]. ===Toronto Raptors (2024–2025)=== On June 28, 2024, Mitchell, [[Aleksandar Vezenkov|Sasha Vezenkov]], the draft rights to [[Jamal Shead]] and a 2025 second-round draft pick were traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[Jalen McDaniels]]. {{cite web|title=RAPTORS COMPLETE TRADE WITH KINGS|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-complete-trade-with-kings|website=NBA.com|date=June 28, 2024|access-date=June 28, 2024}} ===Miami Heat (2025–present)=== On February 6, 2025, Mitchell was traded to the [[Miami Heat]] in a five-team trade, including [[Jimmy Butler]] to the Warriors.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-wiggins-anderson-and-mitchell|title=HEAT ACQUIRE WIGGINS, ANDERSON AND MITCHELL|date=February 6, 2025|website=nba.com}} In 30 appearances (15 starts) for Miami, he averaged 10.3 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 5.3 assists. On April 20, during the first round of the playoffs, Mitchell recorded 18 points, four rebounds and nine assists in a 121–100 Game 1 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web |date=April 20, 2025 |title=Mitchell, Jerome help Cavaliers rout Heat 121-100 in Game 1 of 1st-round series |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401767816 |access-date=March 28, 2025 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} On July 8, 2025, Mitchell re-signed with the Heat on a two-year, $24 million contract.{{Cite web|title=Heat bring back Davion Mitchell on reported 2-year, $24 million deal|url=https://www.si.com/mlb/rays/history/tampa-bay-rays-chandler-simpson-ties-franchise-rookie-record-with-13-game-hitting-streak|access-date=September 23,
